requirement_or_question: I13: no silent metadata loss; every capture or restoration gap is a typed in-band record (FidelityReport at capture, ExtractionReport at extraction), because an archive whose fidelity cannot be assessed is worse than an honestly lossy one. Unsupported ACLs, flags and SELinux labels must warn, never vanish, and platforms must report unavailable classes instead of fabricating values.
supersession_note: Repo docs restate I13 and implement it via static per-platform FidelityReport classes plus ExtractionReport free-text notes. Code audit finds undeclared losses: atime/ctime/Linux btime, NTFS ADS/EAs, Linux inode flags, lone hardlink aliases, discarded tar high mode bits, and a fabricated core.executable=false on Windows (see rows timestamp-capture-set-beyond-mtime, ntfs-alternate-data-streams-capture, hardlink-partial-alias-and-windows-detection, executable-bit-capture-on-non-posix-platforms).

requirement_or_question: The metadata model and FidelityReport are not deferred from v1 (SPEC deliverables 10 and 11 map to §10 and §11), while complete metadata fidelity is explicitly not guaranteed because no target restores every source platform's metadata. requirement_or_question: Timestamps are signed 64-bit seconds plus unsigned 32-bit nanoseconds, never floating point, with source precision and a restorable flag (Timestamp record type 9, tags 1-4); nanoseconds at or above 1e9 are noncanonical, and core.mtime stores one Timestamp record. The widths cover statx (s64 seconds, u32 nanoseconds) and NTFS FILETIME (100 ns since 1601).

research_needed: Canonical vectors for pre-epoch, pre-1601 and far-future values and FILETIME extremes (none in posix-metadata-v1-vectors.txt); independent-reader recomputation.

requirement_or_question: Each timestamp records source precision (1 Second, 2 Centisecond, 3 Microsecond, 4 Hectonanosecond, 5 Nanosecond) so round trips neither invent precision nor create spurious diffs. The enum lacks two-second (FAT/DOS), millisecond, hour (NTFS atime) and unknown classes. Tar import maps 0/2/6/7/9 fractional digits and reports other counts, refusing more than nine; 7z FILETIME maps at 100 ns; cross-precision comparison is unspecified.
superseding_authority: docs/security-metadata-v1.md §Windows descriptor and attributes L128; docs/tar-import-v1.md L58-62; code:crates/entrybound/src/eam/model.rs:100-108

decision_needed: Which precision values does the registry include and how are out-of-registry legacy precisions handled?

requirement_or_question: Restorability is recorded per timestamp so a captured but unrestorable time (e.g. Linux birth time) is declared rather than dropped or falsely restored. Repo carries both Timestamp.restorable and a registry-fixed per-name restorability (Restorable or CaptureOnly, no PlatformSpecific) with nothing tying them together; epoch, time scale, leap-second and zone-less local-time semantics are unstated.
supersession_note: Whether per-item or per-name restorability is authoritative is owned by cross-cluster decision model:critical-metadata-and-restorability; this row keeps the timestamp time-scale question.
research_needed: Independent-reader ambiguity log for time scale; vectors pairing CaptureOnly names with restorable flags.
decision_needed: What epoch/time scale is normative and is Timestamp.restorable retained?

requirement_or_question: Timestamp fidelity is a per-filesystem property recorded per archive, not assumed from the platform: 128-byte ext4 inodes give seconds to 2038 with no crtime, 256-byte inodes nanoseconds to 2446; XFS bigtime reaches 2486; FILETIME counts 100 ns. btrfs, ReFS and APFS encodings and the mkfs.xfs bigtime default are unverified. Native capture never detects filesystem type and tags every non-Windows mtime Nanosecond.
supersession_note: Code contradicts SPEC §10.4 L1266 by deriving precision from the OS (cfg!(windows)) and leaving FidelityReport.filesystem empty.

Read btrfs and APFS on-disk references; test safe detection (statfs f_type, volume information).
decision_needed: Should capture record filesystem type and per-filesystem granularity, and how is it detected safely?

requirement_or_question: Native capture records core.mtime plus Windows creation time (Restorable) and macOS birthtime (CaptureOnly); atime, ctime and Linux statx birth time are neither captured nor declared unavailable. Restoration sets only mtime (out-of-range values reported). NTFS atime has one-hour resolution and atime is volatile; SPEC asserts no Linux syscall sets birth time; 7z creation/access times stay LOM/FidelityReport evidence.

requirement_or_question: Windows creation time is captured by default as AUX metadata, so reversing file creation order keeps LAI and PCR equal but can change container bytes for logically identical trees. EROFS makes per-file mtime optional as a determinism affordance, and R1 argues determinism requires discarding ownership, times and most permission bits via declared lossy policies. The AUX churn cost of volatile times is unmeasured.
supersession_note: Cross-cluster: identity participation and AUX canonicalization are owned by model:identity-v1-metadata-participation and model:aux-determinism-and-canonicalization; this row asks whether volatile times belong in default capture.
research_needed: Repeat-pack experiments on NTFS copies (robocopy, Explorer copy, git checkout) measuring AUX and container differences; verify EROFS COMPAT_MTIME semantics in erofs_fs.h.
decision_needed: Should default packing capture Windows creation time and other volatile times?

requirement_or_question: Where a build epoch is supplied, SPEC says the correct semantic is clamping (no timestamp later than the epoch), not setting. Incumbents diverge on seven magic constants and three semantics (set, clamp, floor), and flat canonical times break relative-mtime consumers (strip-nondeterminism skews .clj older than .class). How an epoch reaches pack given 'never read environment', and whether clamping is a declared loss, are open.
supersession_note: SPEC supersedes R2 survey. Cross-cluster: model:timestamp-normalization-clamp-order-preserving and decision model:canonical-normalization-profiles own the normalization choice. R2 heading says six constants but lists seven answers (editorial).
implementation_evidence: none found (no SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH or clamp option in crates/)
research_needed: Confirm reproducible-builds SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH clamp wording; survey tools depending on relative mtimes (make, Clojure, Python .pyc).
decision_needed: See model decision canonical-normalization-profiles.

requirement_or_question: Frozen exports: ZIP writes a UTC-derived two-second DOS time (silently clamped to 1980-2107) plus a 0x5455 signed 32-bit mtime; subsecond truncation and out-of-range clamping are LOSSY. tar/pax writes ustar octal or canonical pax decimals by precision and refuses precision-inconsistent values; absent mtime becomes 1980-01-01 or 0. Values must never wrap; reader handling of UTC DOS fields and negative fractional pax is unevidenced.
superseding_authority: docs/zip-export-v1.md §Metadata and timestamp contract L39-47; docs/tar-export-v1.md §pax and timestamps L35-46
supersession_note: Repo docs freeze behaviour satisfying R1 Tier 3 no-wrap constraint (clamp with LOSSY report for ZIP, exact pax for tar).
research_needed: Cross-reader matrix (Windows shell, macOS Archive Utility, Info-ZIP, 7-Zip, Python, Java, .NET, GNU tar, bsdtar, Go) for exported pre-1980, post-2038, post-2107 and negative fractional times.
decision_needed: Should a future ZIP profile add NTFS 0x000a or 64-bit times, and are negative fractional pax values interoperable?

requirement_or_question: ZIP import records core.mtime only from CRC/structure-bound UTC extended (0x5455) or NTFS timestamps and core.executable only from compatible Unix mode evidence. DOS local timestamps lack a UTC offset, so they are retained as evidence and reported as unavailable mtime; ZIPs with only DOS times (plausibly common from Windows shell, Java and .NET producers) import with no core.mtime, and prevalence is unmeasured.
supersession_note: Repo docs freeze the no-guess rule (I18). Cross-cluster: legacy-zip decision zip-dos-timestamp-and-extra-time-policy owns the DOS-time import choice.

research_needed: Corpus measurement of ZIPs lacking UTC timestamp extras by producer; user-impact study of missing mtime after import.

requirement_or_question: Tar import maps mode & 0o7777 to posix.mode, numeric uid/gid to posix.uid/gid, any execute bit to core.executable and hardlinks to canonical groups, silently discarding file-type bits above 0o7777. Exports report mode, ownership, hardlinks, xattrs and sparse maps as METADATA_UNSUPPORTED; ZIP export fixes 0644/0755 (directories 040644/040755), tar export fixes directories at 0755. Windows-authored ZIPs must not invent 0755; java.util.zip cannot carry modes at all.

requirement_or_question: posix.mode stores only bits 0o7777 (permissions, setuid, setgid, sticky); file-type bits are noncanonical on decode while model constructors silently mask them. When core.executable and posix.mode are both present they must agree (executable iff any 0o111 bit), else EB_EAM_INVALID_POSIX_METADATA, a reason code no test asserts. Ecosystems such as wheels depend on exact modes for scripts and shared libraries.

Repo extraction always applies recorded posix.mode (including 0o6000 and sticky, no umask) after optional chown, with no policy field or CLI opt-in; docs order chown before chmod precisely so setuid/setgid survive, and a unit test asserts 0o6750 is restored.

requirement_or_question: Archive diff classifies mode, uid/gid, hardlink group, xattr and sparse-map changes as AUXILIARY while core.executable is SEMANTIC; inspection reports POSIX metadata as RECORDED, platform/policy restorability as a DERIVED conclusion, and sparse extents and hardlink group IDs as typed auxiliary facts. Whether an executable-bit flip that also changes mode yields one SEMANTIC record or records in both tiers is unstated.

requirement_or_question: Unix capture records numeric posix.uid/gid only (no names, SIDs or idmap context); restoration is opt-in, applies fchown on the open handle, refuses the u32::MAX sentinel and reports failures. No lossless uid-SID mapping exists, local SIDs are machine-specific, idmapped mounts add three ID spaces, and unprivileged extraction (OSTree bare-user) must still verify identity; cross-platform ownership restore is policy, not a representable value.
supersession_note: Repo realises SPEC ownership opt-in via OwnershipPolicy::Ignore default and --restore-owner. Ecosystems diverge: OCI/deb/rpm override uid/gid, Nix/Git remove ownership.

requirement_or_question: AclV1 (type 40: dialect POSIX1E=1 or NFS4=2, scope ACCESS=1 or DEFAULT=2, ordered AclEntryV1 type 41) carries ACE type ALLOW/DENY/AUDIT/ALARM, principal registry 1-10 (USER_OBJ through UUID), optional uid/gid or 16-byte UUID, u32 permissions and flags. POSIX1E ACEs are ALLOW with zero flags and READ=1, WRITE=2, EXECUTE=4; NFS4 preserves ACE order, uses masks 0x001f01ff and 0x000000ff, and unknown bits fail closed.
supersession_note: Repo docs freeze the wire form (SPEC gives no ACL encoding).

requirement_or_question: A present security.acls item holds 1-3 ACLs with unique sorted (dialect, scope) pairs, each 1-65,536 ACEs; DEFAULT scope is Directory-only and NFS4 is ACCESS-only; a POSIX1E ACCESS ACL requires posix.mode with USER_OBJ, MASK (else GROUP_OBJ) and OTHER equal to the mode classes. Bounds are unmeasured against filesystem ACL limits, and POSIX1E plus NFS4 on one Entry is permitted with no precedence or restore semantics.

requirement_or_question: Under feature 0x10000 Linux reads system.posix_acl_access (and directory _default) with xattr 1.6.1 no-follow calls, parses the little-endian version-2 kernel format independently, remaps Linux read/execute bits to the canonical registry and omits both xattrs from posix.xattrs; archives without the feature keep them as exact xattrs. errno 1/13/45/61/95 marks the class unavailable; a malformed value aborts the pack, a fate the docs never state.
supersession_note: platform-fidelity-v1 refines posix-metadata-v1 (feature 0x10000). APPX recommends explicit little-endian decoding, which the parser follows.

DEFAULT ACL restoration on directories and its interaction with the final mode are untested.

requirement_or_question: Restore order is semantically load-bearing: with a POSIX ACL mask, chmod and set-ACL interact, so SPEC fixes ACLs last after permission bits. Repo docs instead freeze ownership, xattrs, ACLs, final mode, then timestamps, applying directory metadata deepest-first after descendants exist and symlinks last; the mode-ACL consistency invariant presumably makes chmod after ACL equivalent, but no filesystem test covers masks, default ACLs or read-only directories.

requirement_or_question: windows.security-descriptor (type 42) stores exact validated self-relative descriptor bytes (20 B to 1 MiB, revision 1, SE_SELF_RELATIVE, aligned non-overlapping owner/group/DACL/SACL, no trailing bytes); SDDL is only annotation because conditional ACEs and resource attributes use a separate grammar. Docs never enumerate the v1 ACE registry; code accepts ACE types 0x00-0x15 including object, callback, mandatory-label, resource-attribute, scoped-policy and trust-label ACEs.

requirement_or_question: No build captures or restores Windows owner/group SIDs, DACLs or SACLs: capture declares windows.security-descriptor unavailable (no audited safe wrapper exposes exact bytes), Restore reports no audited safe API, and no lossy ACL view or local unsafe FFI is substituted. Windows packs carry only attributes, creation time, mtime and content; SACL absence caused by capture privilege must be declared, not guessed.

requirement_or_question: windows.file-attributes accepts mask 0x005af9a7 (READONLY through RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS), NORMAL only alone, never DEVICE, VIRTUAL, EA or RECALL_ON_OPEN; capture via cap-std masks out DIRECTORY, SPARSE_FILE and REPARSE_POINT. Docs call attributes and creation time Restorable when permitted, yet Restore reports platform metadata unavailable; ENCRYPTED/COMPRESSED (EFS, NTFS compression), cloud OFFLINE/PINNED/RECALL bits and READONLY/SYSTEM semantics are undefined.
supersession_note: Tension between security-metadata-v1 L62-63 (Restorable) and platform-fidelity-v1 L64-66 plus code (restoration unavailable); code is current state.

requirement_or_question: key generate-signing writes Ed25519 secret keys with exclusive create and sync and restricts them to 0600 on Unix only; on Windows the restriction is a no-op, and identity and signing-key files are checked for group/other readability only on Unix, so Windows secret files inherit directory ACLs unchecked.
research_needed: Inspect default inherited ACLs of user-profile folders; safe-Rust options to set owner-only DACLs; practice of ssh-keygen, age and minisign on Windows.
decision_needed: Must the CLI restrict or check secret-key ACLs on Windows?

requirement_or_question: macos.flags accepts the frozen Darwin UF/SF mask 0x40bf80ef, unknown bits failing closed; restoring system and kernel-managed flags (SF immutable/append/restricted/firmlink/dataless, UF_COMPRESSED, UF_DATAVAULT) is privileged or dangerous and no restorable subset exists. Linux statx attribute and inode flags (immutable, append, nodump, compressed, encrypted, verity, DAX) are neither captured nor declared unavailable.

Reference behaviour: ditto preserves forks, HFS metadata, xattrs and ACLs by default; Apple Archive preserves ownership, permissions, flags, times, xattrs, ACLs, APFS compression, clones and sparse files as first-class fields, the highest macOS fidelity baseline, though without an official format spec.

requirement_or_question: The macOS filesystem-compression attribute (com.apple.decmpfs) is CaptureOnly opaque data and never synthesised, because Apple publishes no specification (only ditto --hfsCompression tooling; implementations are reverse-engineered). Whether compressed files are captured as decompressed content with the attribute dropped and loss declared, or as an opaque blob, is undecided; the repo has no decmpfs name or handling beyond recording UF_COMPRESSED in macos.flags.

requirement_or_question: posix.xattrs keeps accessible xattrs exact (empty and binary values valid) with at most 4096 per Entry and 16 MiB per value, via the unix-only xattr =1.6.1 crate (no-follow list/get; FileExt on restore); non-unix reports posix.xattrs unavailable. The 16 MiB bound is unmeasured and exceeds SPEC's 64 KiB citation; a 64 KiB XFS value cannot be restored to ext4, and restore failures are reported per xattr.
supersession_note: Repo bound (16 MiB) supersedes SPEC §10.7 L1294 (255-byte names, 64 KiB values) without cited measurement.

requirement_or_question: SELinux label (security.selinux) format and restore semantics (preserve versus relabel) are unresearched. Linux capture records every accessible xattr exactly, including security.selinux, security.ima, security.capability and trusted.* when privileged, and XAttrPolicy::Restore writes them all back with no namespace filter, so --xattrs restore can grant file capabilities much as setuid does.

requirement_or_question: Repo posix.sparse-map (SparseMapV1 type 38, extents type 39) is AUX-only topology over full plaintext: File-only, logical size equal to content length, at most 1,000,000 ordered nonoverlapping nonadjacent nonzero extents, and every declared hole byte verified zero in INDEXED, STREAM (at EOF) and random reads. SPEC's final disposition was holes-as-chunks with a no-digest sparse hint; sparse maps are an allocation and zip-bomb-by-hole vector.

requirement_or_question: Linux capture reopens each regular file and walks SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE via rustix (never inferring holes from zeros), records a map even for dense files, marks the class unavailable on EINVAL/ENOTSUP and treats non-progress as SourceUnstable; macOS, BSDs and Windows declare posix.sparse-map unavailable. Filesystems need not report holes accurately, so maps are non-canonical; FIEMAP is diagnostic only, and NTFS allocated-range queries and ReFS remain unexplored.

The Unix round-trip test checks only logical length, not reduced allocation, and skips xattr assertions when setting the test xattr fails, so sparse and xattr restoration can go unverified in CI.

requirement_or_question: Hardlinks are ordinary File Entries sharing one ContentObject plus a canonical group digest; equal files without it are not hardlinks, and equal digests never imply topology. A group needs at least two members, one membership per Entry and identical inode-scoped metadata, checked at capture (disagreement is source instability) and in validation (CORRUPT on wrong id). Docs never enumerate which names are inode-scoped.
supersession_note: Group-id construction is owned by cross-cluster decision model:hardlink-group-id-construction (model:hardlink-group-canonical-id).
research_needed: Extract the comparison set from validate.rs and freeze it; negative vectors (singleton group, divergent metadata, conflicting digests); per-platform per-link versus per-inode attributes (NTFS).
decision_needed: Which metadata names are inode-scoped for hardlink agreement?

requirement_or_question: A file with nlink>1 whose other links lie outside the packed root gets no group and no fidelity note: it is captured as an ordinary File, silently losing link topology. On Windows hardlink detection returns None and the report lists 'posix ownership/mode/hardlinks' unavailable, although NTFS supports hard links identifiable by file IDs.
research_needed: Pack a subtree containing one alias of an nlink>1 file; Windows safe API for volume serial plus file index; prevalence of partial groups in backups.
decision_needed: Should lone aliases be declared and Windows links detected?

requirement_or_question: Hardlinks targeting outside the destination must be rejected (R1 Tier 1). In Entrybound a hardlink is content sharing between archive Entries, so extraction links a representative created inside the confined root to other in-root paths; the property holds by construction but lacks an adversarial conformance case against incumbents' observed outcomes.
supersession_note: SPEC I23 (hardlinks as content sharing) makes out-of-destination link targets unrepresentable, superseding R1's validation framing.
research_needed: Conformance corpus case (tar/ZIP hardlink escapes imported, then extracted) with observed-outcome matrix across incumbents and Entrybound.

Socket restoration meaning, device major/minor width across dev_t splits, and omit-and-report versus refuse are undecided.

requirement_or_question: Device nodes are not created by default and need explicit policy plus privilege; FIFOs and sockets need explicit policy (Python's data filter refuses them), and the choice must be documented. An archive may declare that it contains device nodes so callers can refuse early, but the declaration grants nothing and must be validated against actual entries. Because the repo cannot represent these entries, extraction gating is currently vacuous.

requirement_or_question: NTFS alternate data streams and extended attributes are never captured on Windows and are not listed as unavailable (non-unix reports only posix.xattrs), yet SPEC §11.7 restores ADS by default with a disabling policy, and R1 demands an explicit preserve, strip or materialize policy for ADS and AppleDouble files. No registry name, EntryKind or identity placement exists for named streams.

The repo neither reads the archive's own origin marker nor writes markers on extracted files; quarantine survives only as an exact xattr on macOS.

requirement_or_question: Malicious extension metadata must be handled fail-closed and authenticated (criticality bit, feature tiers). Repo metadata items must be Optional in every record version: Critical is refused on decode and never constructed, and unknown names are rejected by the closed registry, so criticality-driven fail-closed behaviour is never exercised.

Repo has no safe-to-copy bit; representation-only repack copies Entry v2/v3 and every POSIX, platform and security record and requires LAI/AUX/PCR equality.
supersession_note: Closed registry makes unknown items undecodable in v1, so SPEC §20.1 L2186 safe-to-copy is unimplemented rather than rejected.

The current build lacks Windows security descriptors, ADS, macOS and NFS4 ACLs, non-Linux sparse capture, special files and atime/ctime, so the 'full' labels are unmeasured and partly contradicted.

requirement_or_question: All platforms capture core.mtime; supported Unix systems also capture core.executable, mode & 0o7777, numeric uid/gid, accessible xattrs and hardlink topology; Linux adds sparse maps and POSIX ACLs, Windows attributes and creation time, macOS flags and birthtime. filesystem-bootstrap.md still says ACLs and platform metadata are unavailable (stale). The round-trip test asserts byte determinism, empty directories, bytes and mtime, and mode only on Unix.

requirement_or_question: Snapshot integration is supported, not required: pack --snapshot uses a platform-consistent snapshot (VSS, APFS, btrfs, ZFS, LVM) where available and records it, and the FidelityReport states snapshot-consistent versus best-effort. The repo has no snapshot option; capture relies on per-file stability checks (only length, mtime and executable on non-Unix) with bounded retries.
supersession_note: No repo authority; SPEC stands.

requirement_or_question: The metadata pass is kernel-unprotected: Landlock cannot restrict chmod, chown, setxattr or utime, and no chmodat2/chownat2 accepts RESOLVE_* flags, so the TOCTOU threat model, including concurrent destination mutation, must be stated explicitly, as only Rust's tar crate does. Repo applies extraction metadata through opened file and directory handles, but capture reads xattrs, ACLs and macOS metadata by ambient path after cap-std traversal.
research_needed: Race tests swapping directories and symlinks during capture and extraction; write the threat-model statement; compare Landlock sandboxing of extraction on WSL.
decision_needed: Should capture use handle-based metadata reads, and is concurrent mutation in the threat model?

requirement_or_question: Containment beats validation: a prefix check models the filesystem and bypasses live in the gap (five node-tar 2021 bypasses; separator-less prefix checks in SharpZipLib and npm decompress; unpatched mholt/archiver; Python's reject-versus-mangle split). On a kernel cannot-prove-containment EAGAIN, retry boundedly then fail hard, never falling back to string validation; RESOLVE_NO_XDEV should be configurable; Docker chrootarchive is correct but privileged.
supersession_note: SPEC adopts R1 doctrine; repo delegates resolution to cap-std, whose retry bound is internal and undocumented.

research_needed: Adversarial rename-race liveness versus DoS measurements; prefix-separator and node-tar bypass cases in the conformance corpus on each OS; bind-mount false-positive frequency for NO_XDEV.
decision_needed: What retry bound and mount-crossing policy apply?

requirement_or_question: CLI publish, repack staging and migration commits write a private sibling, flush it and publish through an exclusive hard link so no existing destination is overwritten. FAT32/exFAT, some SMB/NFS shares and cloud-sync folders lack hard links, so these operations would fail there, and durability beyond flush (directory sync) is unaddressed.
research_needed: Platform matrix on exFAT (Windows host and WSL loop), SMB (Docker Samba), NFS, OneDrive folder; crash-consistency tests with and without directory fsync.
decision_needed: What commit strategy applies where hard links are unavailable?

requirement_or_question: Post-failure disk state must be documented and, in a transactional mode, empty; overwrite handling is a five-way policy that must be exposed. Every surveyed atomic system (dpkg, rpm, OSTree, Nix, containerd, Flatpak, Android A/B) places atomicity above the archive by materializing an opaque object and swapping one pointer. Repo extraction supports only CollisionPolicy::Refuse and has no transactional mode.
supersession_note: R1 §14 item4(e) is in tension with R1 §21 item 8 (transactional mode undecided); repo implements neither transactional extraction nor overwrite modes.
implementation_evidence: crates/entrybound/src/archive/filesystem.rs:568-580 (Refuse only); archive.rs CollisionPolicy has only Refuse
research_needed: Failure-injection experiments during extraction on NTFS and ext4 documenting residual state; incumbent overwrite-policy survey; Task 33 usability.
decision_needed: What failure state and overwrite modes does v1 document and expose?

requirement_or_question: LocalFileRandomReadSource pins a revision only by file length and modification time (None when unavailable) and checks stability only at operation end, so a same-length in-place rewrite with unchanged or coarse mtime (two-second FAT, cached SMB/NFS attributes) is undetectable; stronger platform pins (file IDs, change counters, share-mode locks) are unassessed.
supersession_note: Cross-cluster: requirement and decision access:local-source-revision-detection own the revision-signal choice; this row adds platform timestamp-granularity evidence needs.
research_needed: Platform tests of mtime granularity and availability (NTFS, exFAT, ext4, SMB, NFS) and concurrent-writer detection.

The ZIP adapter refuses a directory declaring non-zero size as EB_ZIP_CONFLICT_DIVERGENCE, but the outcome is unrecorded in the observed-outcome matrix and tar/7z analogues are unchecked.
